The following individuals gave comments in person: 
Cordell Hindler gave comments in support of items N.5.b and N.5.c (Commission on 
Aging appointments).  He expressed concerns regarding the city's vacancy rate and 
suggested allocating funds from the Chevron $550 million settlement for a new 
Compensation and Class Study. 
Don Gosney gave comments opposing the Open Forum public comment time limit as 
established by the City Council's rules. He stated that legislative bodies in other 
jurisdictions allowed more reasonable time limits. 
Claudia Citroen expressed concerns regarding the council's complete knowledge of the 
city's Rent Board operations and the board's lack of reporting like other boards and 
commissions.  She reminded the council that she believed it was her First Amendment 
right to request the removal of Consent Calendar items from the agenda for discussion.  
Ms. Citroen also summarized a list of personal grievances against the city. 
Ivette Blandon reported that she received a citation from security personnel at Booker T. 
Anderson Park while she was legally parked.  She requested that the citation be removed 
from all records and that the matter be investigated.  Ms. Blandon also requested that the 
city's Recreation and Parks Division immediately review its protocols. 
Kimberly Graves expressed concerns regarding the Open Forum public comment time 
limit.  She described her recent traffic stop by Richmond police and the lack of dash 
cameras.  Ms. Graves also expressed concerns regarding racism.

Cassie Levy and Melvin Cifuentes reported that individuals had been illegally occupying 
the property next to their residences since November 2025 and that the property had been 
condemned by the city in December 2025.  They stated that the occupants constituted a 
public nuisance and posed a safety hazard.  Mr. Cifuentes reported that the situation was 
affecting his children and that one of his children had been attacked by an occupant's dog.  
They further stated that the city had not resolved the issue and urged the council to take 
action. 
Mark Wassberg and Irania De La Mora gave comments regarding the 1968 Richmond 
riot.  Ms. De La Mora read an excerpt from a book describing the events surrounding the 
shooting of a teenager, Charles Mims, during the riot. 
Taylor Del Rosarro, Mernard Washington, Shelby Lowry, O'Neill Fernandez, Sean 
Perkins, Daniel Barth, and Neida Pedraza gave comments in support of the services that 
Safe Organized Spaces (SOS) provided to the unhoused community.  They expressed the 
urgent need for SOS funding. 
Diego Garcia expressed concerns regarding the lack of communication with youth-based 
organizations concerning available resources and opportunities.  He stated that Richmond 
SOL, a nonprofit youth soccer organization, was not informed that a fee waiver was 
available to nonprofit organizations for the use of the Richmond Memorial Auditorium.  
Mr. Garcia informed the council that Richmond SOL held its awards ceremony at the 
auditorium in June 2026 and requested reimbursement for the rental fees. 
The following individuals gave comments via teleconference: 
Karina Espino and Loris Mattox gave comments in support of the services provided by 
SOS to the unhoused community.  Ms. Mattox urged the council to prioritize funding for 
SOS and consider establishing a standing budget line item.
